name: Acalabrutinib (covalent BTK inhibitor)

institution.provenance: DRAFT decision-support protocol authored from standard-of-care dosing (experimental; owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

supportiveCare: Continuous oral therapy given until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; the cycle count here is a 28-day accounting frame, not a fixed stop point.
Antiviral prophylaxis per risk; consider PJP prophylaxis with prior purine-analog or steroid exposure.
Avoid concurrent proton-pump inhibitors with the standard capsule formulation (absorption is pH-dependent); separate H2 blockers and antacids in time.
Reconcile CYP3A interactions and antithrombotic agents before starting.
monitoring: Blood pressure and rhythm review for atrial fibrillation at baseline and on treatment
Bleeding-risk review; hold around invasive procedures per practice
CBC periodically; watch for treatment-related lymphocytosis (a redistribution effect, not progression)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 or higher non-hematologic toxicity or grade 4 cytopenia
doseModificationRules.text: Hold until recovery and resume per standard stepwise reduction; physician decides.

drugs.name: Acalabrutinib
drugs.notes: Standard dosing (NCCN / DeVita, general reference): 100 mg by mouth twice daily (about every 12 hours), taken continuously until progression or intolerance. dosePerUnit is the single 100 mg dose; the schedule is twice daily every day of the cycle, shown on day 1 as the accounting anchor. A covalent second-generation BTK inhibitor preferred over first-generation agents for lower atrial-fibrillation and hypertension risk. Own wording; not copied from any source.
